findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There is a gap between the wall and ceiling in the employee restroom. Seal the gap.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
Provide a self-closer for the bathroom door.
6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Remove popcorn ceiling in employee bathroom.
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Director was unable to locate employee health reporting agreements. All staff had copies of signed reporting agreements on file during the 2021 routine inspection. Employee health documents were not available in a designated file and/or employee files. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. Reporting agreement was signed by PIC of food service during inspection. All other staff will review and sign agreements as time allows today. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Chicken Alfredo hot held in two crockpots was observed with internal temperatures of 128F-153F and 127F-149F respectively. Pockets below 135F were thought to be the result of food closer to the lid not getting stirred into the bottom and the need for additional stirring of hot product from the bottom. Chicken Alfredo prep was discussed (see genearl comments for additional information). Prep began around 9am, and all food will be served or discarded before 1pm. Ensure hot foods are marinated at 135F/above throughout the product once heated. Additional time in the microwave may be needed once ingredients are combined prior to hot holding. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival inspector observed handwashing sink being used to rinse a tray, and the basin was later blocked by a plastic tub while ware washing was underway. Proper use and accessibility of handwashing sink was discussed. The kitchen has a 4 basin sink with the far left 1st basin designated for handwashing. When ware washing is occurring, it is recommended to use free flowing water at the 3rd basin used for rinsing dishes rather than standing water, which will also allow the basin to be used for tasks other than handwashing.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 (A) Bleach solution in one of the class rooms was observed at a concentration above 200ppm. Test strip began to bleach out and turn from dark purple to white in color. Solution was diluted during the inspection to be at proper concentration of 200ppm as directed by label instructions. 

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling. Follow label directions and maintain bleach solutions at 200ppm. Use test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Solution for wiping cloth in the kitchen was at 0ppm quat. The solution was prepared earlier in the morning and had not been changed after recent use. Solution was remade at proper concentration of 200ppm quat. 

Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Change the sanitizer solution used for wiping cloth storage in the kitchen as needed during operations, and use test strips to verify proper concentration.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512, & 160 - Cook began to put on gloves without first washing hands. When advised on handwashing prior to putting on gloves, cook noted she washed her hands after using the restroom. However, hands must be re-washed upon entering the kitchen and prior to putting on gloves to handle food and. Cook washed hands and was observed having bare hand contact with the manual faucet prior to drying her hands. Proper technique was discussed. 

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottle of bleach water in the infant room was warm to the touch and had a concentration around 100ppm. Staff were advised on use of test strips to verify concentration is maintained at 200ppm, per label instructions. Staff were also advised on the use of cool water to make solutions; hot water will cause the solution to wear down quicker and lose concentration.

Spray bottle in restroom/changing area was less than 200ppm. Director noted the person that normally changes the solution is off this week, and the bottle was not checked yet today. Solution was leftover from the week prior. Make sure the solution in the restroom is getting checked daily and re-made as needed.

Maintain bleach solutions at 200ppm, and use test strips to verify proper concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottles of bleach water in the infant room and 3-4yr old areas were less than 200ppm chlorine. Clorox bleach used for making spray bottles lists a sanitizing concentration of 200ppm. Bottles of bleach water were remade to be at proper concentration.

Discussed preparation of bleach water bottles with staff and director. All were advised on maintaining the concentration at 200ppm per label instructions and use of test strips to verify the concentration is correct.
NOTE: Depending on the size of the spray bottle used, staff may need to use 20-25ml of bleach (4 or 5 syringes worth when using 5ml syringes) when mixing solutions in full bottles of water.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Concentration of quat solution for ware washing was observed at less than 200ppm. Concentration was between 100-150ppm. Effective concentration range on the product label is 200-400ppm. Solution was prepared within the half hour prior to inspector's arrival; more sanitizer was added to the solution to bring the concentration to 200ppm. Maintain quat solutions at 200-400ppm pre the label instructions.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottle of bleach water in Threes/Preschool room was observed at less than 50ppm chlorine. Teacher stated the bottle would be remade. 

Maintain spray bottles of bleach solutions for wiping surfaces at 100-200ppm chlorine. Use test strips to verify solutions are at proper concentration. Provide chlorine test kits in areas where staff prepare their own bleach solutions, and make sure everyone knows how to properly use test strips.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.8000e - The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) counter under microwave (dust/debris accumulation);
B) bottom inside reach-in freezer (food crumbs);   and
C) small fan on storage shelves (dust accumulation) - will be cleaned before use.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text:
750.1310 - Spray bottles of bleach water and floor cleaner were observed hanging on a shelf above where sliced oranges were prepared and sitting on a small silicone cutting mat in the Toddlers/Twos room. Staff were advised to store chemicals in a different area when food prep/service is occurring. Bottles were moved from the area.
 
All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals. Do not store chemicals over and/or next to foods or food related items (single service articles & clean utensils/dishes).

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed slicing of cheeses and meats for crackers with bare hands. During the inspection, importance of glove use and hand washing was discussed. Make sure that hands are washed and gloves are donned when handling ready-to-eat foods. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed employee use hand to turn off faucet after rinsing. Leave water running and dry hands with paper towel. Use towel to turn off water. A barrier between your clean hands and the soiled faucet should always be used when washing hands. The faucet was just soiled with your dirty hands as you turned on the water. Do not touch clean hands to faucet. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 Certified food manager was not present during the start of the inspection. She was not scheduled for work today. She showed by the end of the inspection. The kitchen manager is planning to take the course soon. I cannot stress enough the importance of taking this course as soon as possible.  All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed a wet wiping cloth being stored on the counter behind the handsink faucet. Discussed storage of cloth during the inspection. Store cloth so it is fully submerged in 200 ppm Steramine or 100ppm Cl. Keep cloth in sanitizing solution between uses.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Observed a cup holding a knife with a dusty base. Clean the cup storing the knives. ALSO, serving utensils are observed stored improperly in a storage container. Store utensils with the handle presented out of the container so your hand will contact the handle and not the portion of the utenil that touches food. Invert utensils. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The refrigerators are observed to have food splash and spills beneath the lower storage bins (back room and kitchen). Clean the interior of the fridges. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 160: Observed a cup being used as a scoop in a Chex Mix container. Cease using cups for scooping. Use a proper scoop or a spoon - present the handle out of food so your hand does not touch the food product.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 650: Observed the plastic bowl holding hamburgers to be seriously pitted from heating within the microwave. Cease use of this pitted plastic bowl. Remove from facility and service. Discussed using the ceramic crock-pot containers already present in facility.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 1210: The wall around the 4-part sink as well as the bathroom (to the right as you walk in) has spots where the paint is peeling. Paint the walls so surfaces are smooth, easily cleanable, and in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed foam padding around drain boards and on shelves within the kitchen. Cease use of foam as it retains moisture and becomes a possible breeding ground for molds and mildew. The velcro on the back room cooler is soiled and peeling. Finally, the roll cart in the kitchen has a piece of wood with tape around the edges. Cease use of tape. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The inside of the refrigerator within the kitchen is soiled with accumulated food crumbs. Clean the inside of the fridge. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 An unlabled bottle of stearamine was observed beneath the kitchen sinks. During inspection, the bottle was properly labeled. Label all chemicals and foods once removed from original packaging. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleansable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices. Cutting boards are starting to show ware with score marks and rough groves on the surfaces. Repair or replace cutting boards.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Cutting boards are draining on the back of the sinks behind faucets.  Air dry the cutting boards away from potential splash contamination (on rolling cart or table behind door) and store properly.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. Refrigeration unit in baby room does not have a thermometer. Provide thermometer for this refrigeration unit.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use or any time that it may have become contaminated. The shelf in the baby room freezer holding teether rings is soiled. Clean by wash, rinse, sanitize and maintain clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  The wall at the end of the galley is scuffed and the ceiling has areas where it is not sealed to the walls. Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Utensils are observed to be stored in bins in the drawer that are soiled.  Wash, rinse and sanitize the bins and utensils stored in the bins. Maintain free of soil.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. The single use utensils are stored in bins that are soiled. Wash rinse and sanitize the bins and discard utensils that have been soiled.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. The wall next to the sink has areas that are in disrepair and need sealed. Seal wall.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
